pace_offset_s.note: the level of the car's clean long-run laps against the field's own compound/age trend; negative is quicker than the field.  It is confounded by the run programme - practice long runs differ in fuel load and in how hard they are being driven, and neither is observable here - so it is reported, not charged: no cost in the objective reads it (see car_terms)

deg_rate_by_compound.note: the field rate plus the fit's own dev[d, c], pooled driver -> team by percar.team_pooled_dev at k = 20 clean laps; the team -> field step is the fit's own hierarchical pull on dev (sigma_dev ~ HalfNormal(0.02)) and is not applied twice here

age_sensitivity.note: the same pooled deviation as one number: how much more lap time per lap of tyre age this car gives away than the field

warmup_s.note: mean excess of laps 1/2 of a stint over that stint's own trend (fitted from lap 3); in a practice table lap 1 is the out-lap and is filtered out, so this is normally the first flying lap.  A pool of fewer than 2 stints contributes nothing

consistency_s.note: residual SD about the stint trend, over the laps the trend was fitted on

traffic_sensitivity.note: the car's excess over the stint trend within 2 s of the car ahead, divided by the field's same excess (0.239 s/lap over 38 laps); 1.0 is a car that loses what everyone loses

push_response.note: not identifiable pre-race: a practice long run is a full-push experiment by construction, so this weekend carries no within-car variation in push from which a per-car management response could be estimated.  The calibrated team/field value is used, fully shrunk

explanation: OCO: 1-stop M-H @ 18; BEA: 1-stop M-H @ 18 - the same first stop (lap 18); the same plan shape

pace level: OCO -0.348 s/lap vs BEA 0.549 s/lap (-0.897); the quicker car reaches any given gap to the car ahead sooner, which moves the lap its stop is worth taking [OCO: n=14, w=0.64, driver | BEA: n=17, w=0.68, driver]
S1 degradation: OCO +0.0050 vs BEA +0.0690 s/lap of age (-0.0640); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=11, w=0.48, team | BEA: n=18, w=0.60, driver]
S3 degradation: OCO +0.0386 vs BEA +0.0025 s/lap of age (+0.0361); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=11, w=0.48, team | BEA: n=18, w=0.60, driver]
S2 degradation: OCO +0.0032 vs BEA +0.0290 s/lap of age (-0.0258); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=11, w=0.48, team | BEA: n=18, w=0.60, driver]

consistency: OCO 1.08 s vs BEA 0.61 s (+0.467); a wider spread about the stint trend is uncertainty, not a cost: it widens the window rather than moving the lap [OCO: n=10, w=0.45, team | BEA: n=15, w=0.56, driver]

race-history rate factor (from previous races, not this weekend's evidence): OCO x1.069 vs BEA x1.189 after precision shrinkage (raw x1.120 / x1.318, ln_sd 0.08357436962967356 / 0.07723749666602743); it scales the whole rate, so the higher factor stops earlier
the two recommendations agree: the differences above are not big enough to separate the plans
